answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a stake bond before earning trust. Creating thousands of fake identities then becomes expensive, because every mirror copy of an identity must pay its own bond, and misbehavior burns it. A shared reputation ledger acts as a haven where honest agents accumulate history that cannot be cloned for free, while a walnut-shell puzzle that is cheap to verify but costly to mass-produce throttles bulk account creation. Attackers face real capital loss and compute cost, while legitimate agents pay once and keep their standing.
